<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><A NAME="a_GLOSSARY_OF_OIL_1"></A><A NAME="a_GLOSSARY_OF_OIL"></A>GLOSSARY OF OIL AND NATURAL GAS TERMS</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">The following are abbreviations
and definitions of certain terms used in this Report, which are commonly used in the oil and natural industry.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>AFE</U></I>&nbsp;</B>or<B>&nbsp;<I><U>Authorization
for Expenditures</U></I></B>. A document that lays out proposed expenses for a particular project and authorizes an individual
or group to spend a certain amount of money for that project.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I>ARO</I></B>.
Asset retirement obligation, a legal obligation associated with the retirement of an asset, which in the Company&rsquo;s case is
generally associated with the pugging of oil wells.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Bbl</U></I></B>.
One stock tank barrel, or 42 U.S. gallons liquid volume, used in this Annual Report in reference to crude oil or other liquid hydrocarbons.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Bcf</U></I></B>.&nbsp;An
abbreviation for billion cubic feet. Unit used to measure large quantities of gas, approximately equal to 1 trillion Btu.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Boe</U></I></B>.
Barrels of oil equivalent, determined using the ratio of one Bbl of crude oil, condensate or natural gas liquids, to six Mcf of
natural gas.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Boepd</U></I></B>.
Barrels of oil equivalent per day.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Bopd</U></I></B>.
Barrels of oil per day.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Btu</U></I></B>
or <B><I><U>British thermal unit</U></I></B>. The quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of one pound of water by one
degree Fahrenheit.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Completion</U></I></B>.
The operations required to establish production of oil or natural gas from a wellbore, usually involving perforations, stimulation
and/or installation of permanent equipment in the well or, in the case of a dry hole, the reporting of abandonment to the appropriate
agency.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Condensate</U></I></B>.
Liquid hydrocarbons associated with the production of a primarily natural gas reserve.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Conventional
resources</U></I></B>. Natural gas or oil that is produced by a well drilled into a geologic formation in which the reservoir and
fluid characteristics permit the natural gas or oil to readily flow to the wellbore.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Developed
acreage</U></I></B>. The number of acres that are allocated or assignable to productive wells.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Development
well</U></I></B>. A well drilled into a proved oil or natural gas reservoir to the depth of a stratigraphic horizon known to be
productive.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Estimated
ultimate recovery</U></I></B> or <B><I><U>EUR</U></I></B>. Estimated ultimate recovery is the sum of reserves remaining as of a
given date and cumulative production as of that date.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Exploratory
well</U></I></B>. A well drilled to find and produce oil or natural gas reserves not classified as proved, to find a new reservoir
in a field previously found to be productive of oil or natural gas in another reservoir or to extend a known reservoir.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Farmin</U></I></B>
or <B><I><U>farmout</U></I></B>. An agreement under which the owner of a working interest in an oil or natural gas lease assigns
the working interest or a portion of the working interest to another party who desires to drill on the leased acreage. Generally,
the assignee is required to drill one or more wells in order to earn its interest in the acreage. The assignor usually retains
a royalty or reversionary interest in the lease. The interest received by an assignee is a &ldquo;<U>farmin</U>&rdquo; while the
interest transferred by the assignor is a &ldquo;<U>farmout.</U>&rdquo;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>FERC</U></I></B>.
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 3; Options: NewSection; Value: 1 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1pt solid"><P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; text-align: center; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->1<!-- Field: /Sequence --></P></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><P STYLE="margin: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><A HREF="#toc" STYLE="font-style: italic">Table of Contents</A></P></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Field</U></I></B>.
An area consisting of a single reservoir or multiple reservoirs all grouped on or related to the same individual geological structural
feature and/or stratigraphic condition.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Gross acres</U></I></B>
or <B><I><U>gross wells</U></I></B>. The total acres or wells in which a working interest is owned.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Henry Hub</U></I></B>.
A natural gas pipeline located in Erath, Louisiana that serves as the official delivery location for futures contracts on the NYMEX.
The settlement prices at the Henry Hub are used as benchmarks for the entire North American natural gas market.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;<B><I><U>Held
by production</U></I></B>. An oil and natural gas property under lease in which the lease continues to be in force after the primary
term of the lease in accordance with its terms as a result of production from the property.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Horizontal
drilling</U></I></B> or <B><I><U>well</U></I></B>. A drilling operation in which a portion of the well is drilled horizontally
within a productive or potentially productive formation. This operation typically yields a horizontal well that has the ability
to produce higher volumes than a vertical well drilled in the same formation. A horizontal well is designed to replace multiple
vertical wells, resulting in lower capital expenditures for draining like acreage and limiting surface disruption.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Liquids</U></I></B>.
Liquids, or natural gas liquids, are marketable liquid products including ethane, propane, butane and pentane resulting from the
further processing of liquefiable hydrocarbons separated from raw natural gas by a natural gas processing facility.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>LOE</U></I></B>&nbsp;or&nbsp;<B><I><U>Lease
operating expenses</U></I></B>. The costs of maintaining and operating property and equipment on a producing oil and gas lease.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>MBbl</U></I></B>.
One thousand barrels of crude oil or other liquid hydrocarbons.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>MMBbl/d</U></I></B>.
One thousand barrels of crude oil or other liquid hydrocarbons per day.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Mcf</U></I></B>.
One thousand cubic feet of natural gas.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Mcfgpd</U></I></B>.
Thousands of cubic feet of natural gas per day.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>MMcf</U></I></B>.
One million cubic feet of natural gas.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>MMBtu</U></I></B>.
One million British thermal units.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Net acres</U></I></B>
or <B><I><U>net wells</U></I></B>. The sum of the fractional working interest owned in gross acres or wells.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Net revenue
interest</U></I></B>. The interest that defines the percentage of revenue that an owner of a well receives from the sale of oil,
natural gas and/or natural gas liquids that are produced from the well.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>NGL</U></I></B>.
Natural gas liquids.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>NYMEX</U></I></B>.
New York Mercantile Exchange.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Permeability</U></I></B>.
A reference to the ability of oil and/or natural gas to flow through a reservoir.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Petrophysical
analysis</U></I></B>. The interpretation of well log measurements, obtained from a string of electronic tools inserted into the
borehole, and from core measurements, in which rock samples are retrieved from the subsurface, then combining these measurements
with other relevant geological and geophysical information to describe the reservoir rock properties.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Play</U></I></B>.
A set of known or postulated oil and/or natural gas accumulations sharing similar geologic, geographic and temporal properties,
such as source rock, migration pathways, timing, trapping mechanism and hydrocarbon type.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Possible reserves</U></I></B>.
Additional reserves that are less certain to be recognized than probable reserves.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 4; Value: 1 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1pt solid"><P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; text-align: center; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->2<!-- Field: /Sequence --></P></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><P STYLE="margin: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><A HREF="#toc" STYLE="font-style: italic">Table of Contents</A></P></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Probable reserves</U></I></B>.
Additional reserves that are less certain to be recognized than proved reserves but which, in sum with proved reserves, are as
likely as not to be recovered.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Producing
well, production well</U></I></B> or <B><I><U>productive well</U></I></B>. A well that is found to be capable of producing hydrocarbons
in sufficient quantities such that proceeds from the sale of the well&rsquo;s production exceed production-related expenses and
taxes.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Properties</U></I></B>.
Natural gas and oil wells, production and related equipment and facilities and natural gas, oil or other mineral fee, leasehold
and related interests.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Prospect</U></I></B>.
A specific geographic area which, based on supporting geological, geophysical or other data and also preliminary economic analysis
using reasonably anticipated prices and costs, is considered to have potential for the discovery of commercial hydrocarbons.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Proved developed
reserves</U></I></B>. Proved reserves that can be expected to be recovered through existing wells and facilities and by existing
operating methods.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Proved reserves</U></I></B>.
Reserves of oil and natural gas that have been proved to a high degree of certainty by analysis of the producing history of a reservoir
and/or by volumetric analysis of adequate geological and engineering data.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Proved undeveloped
reserves</U></I></B> or <B><I><U>PUDs</U></I></B>. Proved reserves that are expected to be recovered from new wells on undrilled
acreage or from existing wells where a relatively major expenditure is required for recompletion.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Repeatability</U></I></B>.
The potential ability to drill multiple wells within a prospect or trend.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Reservoir</U></I></B>.
A porous and permeable underground formation containing a natural accumulation of producible oil and/or natural gas that is confined
by impermeable rock or water barriers and is individual and separate from other reservoirs.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Royalty interest</U></I></B>.
An interest in an oil and natural gas lease that gives the owner of the interest the right to receive a portion of the production
from the leased acreage (or of the proceeds of the sale thereof), but generally does not require the owner to pay any portion of
the costs of drilling or operating the wells on the leased acreage. Royalties may be either landowner&rsquo;s royalties, which
are reserved by the owner of the leased acreage at the time the lease is granted, or overriding royalties, which are usually reserved
by an owner of the leasehold in connection with a transfer to a subsequent owner.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0 5.8pt 0 5.5pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 28.75pt"><B><I><U>Shut
in</U></I></B><I>. </I>To shut in a well is to close off the well so that it stops producing.<B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>





<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>2-D seismic</U></I></B>.
The method by which a cross-section of the earth&rsquo;s subsurface is created through the interpretation of reflecting seismic
data collected along a single source profile.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>3-D seismic</U></I></B>.
The method by which a three-dimensional image of the earth&rsquo;s subsurface is created through the interpretation of reflection
seismic data collected over a surface grid. 3-D seismic surveys allow for a more detailed understanding of the subsurface than
do 2-D seismic surveys and contribute significantly to field appraisal, exploitation and production.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Trend</U></I></B>.
A region of oil and/or natural gas production, the geographic limits of which have not been fully defined, having geological characteristics
that have been ascertained through supporting geological, geophysical or other data to contain the potential for oil and/or natural
gas reserves in a particular formation or series of formations.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Unconventional
resource play</U></I></B>. A set of known or postulated oil and or natural gas resources or reserves warranting further exploration
which are extracted from (a) low-permeability sandstone and shale formations and (b) coalbed methane. These plays require the application
of advanced technology to extract the oil and natural gas resources.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 5; Value: 1 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1pt solid"><P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; text-align: center; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->3<!-- Field: /Sequence --></P></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><P STYLE="margin: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><A HREF="#toc" STYLE="font-style: italic">Table of Contents</A></P></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Undeveloped
acreage</U></I></B>. Lease acreage on which wells have not been drilled or completed to a point that would permit the production
of commercial quantities of oil and natural gas, regardless of whether such acreage contains proved reserves. Undeveloped acreage
is usually considered to be all acreage that is not allocated or assignable to productive wells.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Unproved and
unevaluated properties</U></I></B>. Refers to properties where no drilling or other actions have been undertaken that permit such
property to be classified as proved.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Vertical well</U></I></B>.
A hole drilled vertically into the earth from which oil, natural gas or water flows are pumped.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Volumetric
reserve analysis</U></I></B>. A technique used to estimate the amount of recoverable oil and natural gas. It involves calculating
the volume of reservoir rock and adjusting that volume for the rock porosity, hydrocarbon saturation, formation volume factor and
recovery factor.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Wellbore</U></I></B>.
The hole made by a well.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>WTI</U></I></B>&nbsp;or&nbsp;<B><I><U>West
Texas Intermediate</U></I></B>. A grade of crude oil used as a benchmark in oil pricing. This grade is described as light because
of its relatively low density, and sweet because of its low sulfur content.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B><I><U>Working interest</U></I></B>.
The operating interest that gives the owner the right to drill, produce and conduct operating activities on the property and receive
a share of production.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">PART I</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: italic bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><A NAME="a_Mid-Continent_Acquisition_and"></A><A NAME="item1"></A><A NAME="a_ITEM_1__BUSINESS_"></A>ITEM 1. BUSINESS.</P>

<P STYLE="font: italic bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><A NAME="a_General"></A>General</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Camber Energy, Inc.,
a Nevada corporation, is based in Houston, Texas. We are currently primarily engaged in the acquisition, development and sale of
crude oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids from various known productive geological formations, including the Cline shale and
upper Wolfberry shale in Glasscock County, Texas. Incorporated in Nevada in December 2003 under the name Panorama Investments Corp.,
the Company changed its name to Lucas Energy, Inc., effective June 9, 2006, and effective January 4, 2017, the Company changed
its name to Camber Energy, Inc. After the divestiture of our South Texas properties during fiscal 2019, as discussed in further
detail below under &ldquo;<A HREF="#a_Mid-Continent_Acquisition_and">Mid-Continent Acquisition and Divestiture</A>&rdquo;, we initiated
discussions with several potential acquisition and merger candidates to diversify our operations.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Pursuant to those discussions
on July 8, 2019, we acquired Lineal Star Holdings, LLC (&ldquo;<U>Lineal</U>&rdquo;) pursuant to the terms of an Agreement and
Plan of Merger dated as of the same date (the &ldquo;<U>Lineal Plan of Merger</U>&rdquo; and the merger contemplated therein, the
&ldquo;<U>Lineal Merger</U>&rdquo; or the &ldquo;<U>Lineal Acquisition</U>&rdquo;), by and between Lineal, Camber, Camber Energy
Merger Sub 2, Inc., Camber&rsquo;s wholly-owned subsidiary (&ldquo;<U>Merger Sub</U>&rdquo;), and the Members of Lineal (the &ldquo;<U>Lineal
Members</U>&rdquo;). Lineal is a specialty construction and oil and gas services enterprise providing services to the energy industry.
Pursuant to the Lineal Plan of Merger, Camber acquired 100% of the ownership of Lineal from the Lineal Members in consideration
for newly issued shares of Series E Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock (&ldquo;<U>Series E Preferred Stock</U>&rdquo;) and
Series F Redeemable Preferred Stock (&ldquo;<U>Series F Preferred Stock</U>&rdquo;), as discussed in greater detail below under
&ldquo;<A HREF="#a_Lineal_Acquisition_and">Lineal Acquisition and Divestiture</A>&rdquo;.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">On December 31, 2019,
the Company entered into, and closed the transactions contemplated by a Preferred Stock Redemption Agreement, by and between the
Company, Lineal and the holders of the Company&rsquo;s Series E Preferred Stock and Series F Preferred Stock (the &ldquo;<U>Preferred
Holders</U>&rdquo;). Pursuant to the Redemption Agreement, effective as of December 31, 2019, each holder of Series E Preferred
Stock transferred such Series E Preferred Stock to Camber in consideration for their pro rata share (except as discussed below
in connection with the Series F Preferred Stock holder, who was also a holder of Series E Preferred Stock)&nbsp;of 100% of the
Common Shares of Lineal and the holder of the Series F Preferred Stock transferred such Series F Preferred Stock (and such Series
E Preferred Stock shares held by such holder)&nbsp;to Camber in consideration for 100% of the Preferred Shares of Lineal and as
a result, ownership of 100% of Lineal was transferred back to the Preferred Holders, the original owners of Lineal prior to the
Lineal Merger. Additionally, all of the Series E Preferred Stock and Series F Preferred Stock of the Company were automatically
cancelled and deemed redeemed by the Company and the Series F Holder waived and forgave any and all accrued dividends on the Series
F Preferred Stock. See also &ldquo;<A HREF="#a_Lineal_Acquisition_and">Lineal Acquisition and Divestiture</A>&rdquo; below.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; background-color: white">On
February 3, 2020, the Company entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (as amended to date, the &ldquo;<U>Merger Agreement</U>&rdquo;)
with Viking Energy Group, Inc. (&ldquo;<U>Viking</U>&rdquo;). The Merger Agreement provides that a newly-formed wholly-owned subsidiary
of the Company (&ldquo;<U>Merger Sub</U>&rdquo;) will merge with and into Viking (the &ldquo;<U>Merger</U>&rdquo;), with Viking
surviving the Merger as a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, as described in greater detail below under &ldquo;<A HREF="#a_Viking_Plan_of">Viking
Plan of Merger</A>&rdquo;.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; background-color: white">Moving
forward, the Company plans to complete the Merger with Viking and then focus on growing through the development of Viking&rsquo;s
properties while also seeking new acquisitions to grow its oil and gas production and revenues through the combined entity. The
Company anticipates raising additional financing to complete acquisitions following the closing of the Merger, which may be through
the sale of debt or equity. As described below, the Merger is subject to various closing conditions which may not be met pursuant
to the contemplated timeline, if at all.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: italic 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Mid-Continent Acquisition and
Divestiture</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: italic 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">On December 30, 2015,
the Company entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement (as amended from time to time, the &ldquo;<U>Asset Purchase Agreement</U>&rdquo;)
to acquire, from twenty-three different entities and individuals (the &ldquo;<U>Sellers</U>&rdquo;), working interests in producing
properties and undeveloped acreage (the &ldquo;<U>Acquisition</U>&rdquo;), which acquisition transaction was completed on August
25, 2016. The assets acquired include varied interests in two largely contiguous acreage blocks in the liquids-rich Mid-Continent
region. In connection with the closing of the acquisition, we assumed approximately $30.6 million of commercial bank debt, issued
417 shares of common stock to certain of the Sellers, issued 552,000 shares of Series B Preferred Stock to one of the Sellers and
its affiliate, and paid $4,975,000 in cash to certain of the Sellers. The effective date of the Acquisition was April 1, 2016.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">On July 12, 2018, the
Company entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement (as amended, the &ldquo;<U>Sale Agreement</U>&rdquo;), as seller, with N&amp;B
Energy, LLC (&ldquo;<U>N&amp;B Energy</U>&rdquo;) as purchaser, which entity is affiliated with Richard N. Azar II, the Company&rsquo;s
former Chief Executive Officer and former director, and Donnie B. Seay, the Company&rsquo;s former director (each of which were
Sellers). Pursuant to the Sale Agreement, which closed September 26, 2018, effective August 1, 2018, the Company sold to N&amp;B
Energy a substantial portion of its assets, including all of the assets acquired pursuant to the Acquisition and certain other
assets, other than the production payment and overriding royalty interests discussed below (the &ldquo;<U>Disposed Assets</U>&rdquo;).
In consideration for the Disposed Assets, N&amp;B Energy agreed to pay the Company $100 in cash, to assume the Company&rsquo;s
liabilities and contractual obligations in connection with the Disposed Assets (including lease and bonus payments), to assume
all of the Company&rsquo;s obligations and debt owed under its outstanding loan agreement with International Bank of Commerce (&ldquo;<U>IBC
Bank</U>&rdquo;), which had a then outstanding principal balance of approximately $36.9 million and the other parties agreed to
enter into a settlement agreement.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">On September 26, 2018,
the Company entered into an Assumption Agreement (the &ldquo;<U>Assumption Agreement</U>&rdquo;) with IBC Bank; CE Operating, LLC,
the Company&rsquo;s wholly-owned subsidiary (&ldquo;<U>CE Operating</U>&rdquo;), which became a party to the Sale Agreement pursuant
to the second amendment thereto; N&amp;B Energy; Mr. Azar; RAD2 Minerals, Ltd., an entity owned and controlled by Mr. Azar (&ldquo;<U>RAD2</U>&rdquo;);
Mr. Seay; and DBS Investments, Ltd., an entity owned and controlled by Mr. Seay (&ldquo;<U>DBS</U>&rdquo;). Azar, Seay, RAD2, and
DBS are collectively referred to as the &ldquo;<U>Guarantors</U>&rdquo;.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Pursuant to the Assumption
Agreement, N&amp;B Energy agreed to assume all of the Company&rsquo;s liabilities and obligations owed to IBC Bank and IBC Bank
approved the transactions contemplated by the Sale Agreement and the assumption by N&amp;B Energy of all of the amounts and liabilities
which the Company owed to IBC Bank (collectively, the &ldquo;<U>IBC Obligations</U>&rdquo;). Finally, pursuant to the Assumption
Agreement, IBC Bank released and forever discharged the Company and CE Operating and each of their current and former officers,
directors, and stockholders, from all covenants, agreements, obligations, claims and demands of any kind, whether in law or at
equity, which IBC Bank then had, arising out of or related to the amounts which the Company owed to IBC Bank under the Loan Agreement
or mortgages and/or under such documents or agreements, and further agreed to release the lien which IBC Bank then held on certain
of the Company&rsquo;s properties located in west Texas.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">On September 26, 2018,
the transactions contemplated by the Sale Agreement closed and N&amp;B Energy assumed all of the IBC Obligations (pursuant to the
Assumption Agreement) and paid the Company $100 in cash, and the Company transferred ownership of the Disposed Assets to N&amp;B
Energy.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Notwithstanding the
sale of the Disposed Assets, the Company retained its assets in Glasscock and Hutchinson Counties, Texas and also retained a 12.5%
production payment (effective until a total of $2.5 million has been received, of which no funds have been received to date) and
a 3% overriding royalty interest, in its then existing Okfuskee County, Oklahoma asset; and retained an overriding royalty interest
on certain other undeveloped leasehold interests, pursuant to an Assignment of Production Payment and Assignment of Overriding
Royalty Interests.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">The effective date
of the Sale Agreement was August 1, 2018. The Assets were assigned &ldquo;<U>as is</U>&rdquo; with all faults.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">As a result of the
Assumption Agreement and the Sale Agreement, the Company reduced its liabilities by $37.9 million and its assets by approximately
$12.1 million.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: italic 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U><A NAME="a_Lineal_Acquisition_and"></A>Lineal Acquisition and Divestiture</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: italic 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">In connection with
the Lineal Plan of Merger, the Company entered into several other agreements, including (a)&nbsp;a Security Exchange Agreement
dated July 8, 2019 (the &ldquo;<U>Exchange Agreement</U>&rdquo;), by and between the Company and an accredited institutional investor,
Discover Growth Fund LLC, who has funded the Company over the past several years (&ldquo;<U>Discover</U>&rdquo;); (b)&nbsp;a Termination
Agreement dated July 8, 2019, by and between the Company and Discover Growth Fund, which purchased shares of Series C Preferred
Stock from us in December 2018 (&ldquo;<U>Discover Growth</U>&rdquo;, which subsequently transferred all of its shares of Series
C Preferred Stock to Discover); and (c)&nbsp;a Funding and Loan Agreement dated July 8, 2019, by and among the Company, Lineal,
and certain of the Lineal Members who also acquired shares of the Company&rsquo;s preferred stock as a result of the Lineal Merger
(the &ldquo;<U>Funding Agreement</U>&rdquo;), which provided for the Company to loan $1,050,000 to Lineal, which loan was evidenced
by a Promissory Note entered into by Lineal, as borrower, in favor of the Company, as lender, dated July 8, 2019 (the &ldquo;<U>July
2019 Lineal Note</U>&rdquo;).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Also as part of the
Lineal Merger, the Company designated three new series of preferred stock, (1)&nbsp;Series D Convertible Preferred Stock (the &ldquo;<U>Series
D Preferred Stock</U>&rdquo; and the certificate of designations setting forth the rights thereof, the &ldquo;<U>Series D Designation</U>&rdquo;);
(2)&nbsp;Series E Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock (the &ldquo;<U>Series E Preferred Stock</U>&rdquo; and the certificate
of designation setting forth the rights thereof (the &ldquo;<U>Series E Designation</U>&rdquo;); and (3)&nbsp;Series F Redeemable
Preferred Stock (the &ldquo;<U>Series F Preferred Stock</U>&rdquo; and the certificate of designation setting forth the rights
thereof, the &ldquo;<U>Series F Designation</U>&rdquo;, and the Series E Preferred Stock and the Series F Preferred Stock, collectively,
the &ldquo;<U>Series E and F Preferred Stock</U>&rdquo;). Additionally, with the approval of the holders thereof, the Company amended
and restated the designation of its Series C Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock (the &ldquo;<U>Series C Preferred Stock</U>&rdquo;
and the amended and restated designation setting forth the rights thereof, the &ldquo;<U>Series C Designation</U>&rdquo;).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">The Lineal Plan of
Merger, Series D Designation and Series E Designation, provided that, effective upon the date that the stockholders of the Company
had approved the Lineal Plan of Merger and issuance of shares in connection therewith (the &ldquo;<U>Stockholder Approval</U>&rdquo;
and such date of Stockholder Approval, the &ldquo;<U>Stockholder Approval Date</U>&rdquo;), and subject to certain closing conditions,
(a)&nbsp;the common stock holders of the Company were to hold between 6% and 6.67% of the Company&rsquo;s fully-diluted capitalization
(depending on certain factors); (b)&nbsp;Discover was to hold Series D Preferred Stock convertible into 26.67% of the Company&rsquo;s
fully-diluted capitalization, subject to the terms of the Series D Preferred Stock;&nbsp;and (c)&nbsp;the Lineal Members, who held
the Series E Preferred Stock, were to have the right to convert such Series E Preferred Stock, subject to the terms thereof, as
discussed above, into 66.67% of the Company&rsquo;s fully-diluted capitalization, or 70%, subject to certain factors.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Pursuant to the Lineal
Plan of Merger, Merger Sub merged with and into Lineal, with Lineal continuing as the surviving entity in the Lineal Merger and
as a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">On October 8, 2019,
Lineal acquired an 80% interest in Evercon Energy LLC (&ldquo;<U>Evercon</U>&rdquo;). The acquisition required Lineal to assume
certain liabilities and provide working capital for a period of six months in an amount of $50,000 per month to Evercon. As part
of the Lineal Divestiture, described below, Evercon was divested effective December 31, 2019.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">The Funding Agreement
required the Company to fund $1,050,000 in immediately available funds to Lineal (the &ldquo;<U>Loan</U>&rdquo;). The Loan was
documented by the July 2019 Lineal Note and the Loan was made on July 9, 2019.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Subsequent to the closing
date of the Lineal Plan of Merger, for various reasons, the parties to such Lineal Plan of Merger were unable to complete a further
acquisition or combination which would allow the post-Merger combined company to meet the initial listing standards of the NYSE
American. This was a requirement to the Company having to seek shareholder approval for the terms of the Series E Preferred Stock
(including the voting rights (i.e., the right, together with the Series F Preferred Stock, to vote 80% of the Company&rsquo;s voting
shares) and conversion rights (i.e., the right to convert into between 67-70% of the Company&rsquo;s post-shareholder approval
capitalization) associated therewith). Consequently, and because no definitive timeline was able to be established for when the
Company believed it would meet the NYSE American initial listing standards and consequently, when shareholder approval would be
sought or received for the terms of the Series E Preferred Stock and Series F Preferred Stock, the Preferred Holders and the Company
determined it was in their mutual best interests to unwind the Lineal Merger.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">In order to affect
such unwinding, on December 31, 2019, we, Lineal (and its subsidiaries) and the Preferred Holders entered into, and closed the
transactions contemplated by, a Preferred Stock Redemption Agreement (the &ldquo;<U>Redemption Agreement</U>&rdquo; and the redemption
contemplated thereby, the &ldquo;<U>Redemption</U>&rdquo; or the &ldquo;<U>Lineal Divestiture</U>&rdquo;).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 11; Value: 1 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1pt solid"><P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; text-align: center; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->9<!-- Field: /Sequence --></P></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><P STYLE="margin: 0pt; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><A HREF="#toc" STYLE="font-style: italic">Table of Contents</A></P></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Pursuant to the Redemption
Agreement, the parties thereto mutually agreed to unwind the Lineal Merger and allow for the redemption in full of Lineal by the
Preferred Holders. In connection therewith, the Company redeemed the Company&rsquo;s Series E and F Preferred Stock issued in connection
with the Lineal Merger and ownership of 100% of Lineal was transferred back to the Preferred Holders, and all of the Series E Preferred
Stock and Series F Preferred Stock of the Company outstanding were cancelled through the redemption. &nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">The Redemption Agreement
also provided for (a)&nbsp;the entry by Lineal and the Company into a new unsecured promissory note in the amount of $1,539,719,
the outstanding amount of the July 2019 Lineal Note together with additional amounts loaned by Camber to Lineal through December
31, 2019 (the &ldquo;<U>December 2019 Lineal Note</U>&rdquo;); (b)&nbsp;the unsecured loan by the Company to Lineal on December
31, 2019 of an additional $800,000, entered into by Lineal in favor of the Company on December 31, 2019 (&ldquo;<U>Lineal Note
No. 2</U>&rdquo;); and (c)&nbsp;the termination of the prior Lineal Plan of Merger and Funding Agreement entered into in connection
therewith (pursuant to which all funds previously held in a segregated account for future Lineal acquisitions, less amounts loaned
pursuant to Lineal Note No. 2, were released back to the Company). The December 2019 Lineal Note and Lineal Note No. 2, accrue
interest, payable quarterly in arrears, beginning on March 31, 2020 and continuing until December 31, 2021, when all interest and
principal is due, at 8% and 10% per annum (18% upon the occurrence of an event of default), respectively.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">The divestiture resulting
from the Redemption Agreement qualifies as a discontinued operation in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles
(&ldquo;<U>GAAP</U>&rdquo;). As a result, operating results and cash flows related to the Lineal operations have been reflected
as discontinued operations in the Company&rsquo;s consolidated statements of operations and consolidated statements of cash flows
for the periods presented.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: italic 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U><A NAME="a_Viking_Plan_of"></A>Viking Plan of Merger</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: italic 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; background-color: white">On
February 3, 2020, the Company and Viking entered into the Merger Agreement. <FONT STYLE="color: #212529">Pursuant to the Merger
Agreement, at the effective time of the Merger (the &ldquo;<U>Effective Time</U>&rdquo;), each share of common stock of Viking
(the &ldquo;<U>Viking Common Stock</U>&rdquo;)&nbsp;issued and outstanding, other than certain shares owned by the Company, Viking
and Merger Sub, will be converted into the right to receive the pro rata share of 80% of the Company&rsquo;s post-closing capitalization,
subject to certain adjustment mechanisms discussed in the Merger Agreement (and excluding shares issuable upon conversion of the
Series C Preferred Stock of the Company). Holders of Viking Common Stock will have any fractional shares of Company common stock
after the Merger rounded up to the nearest whole share. The completion of the Merger is subject to certain closing conditions.
Specifically, the percentage of shares retained by Camber shareholders (initially 80%, the &ldquo;<U>Camber Percentage</U>&rdquo;)
is </FONT>adjusted as follows: (i) for each (A) $500,000 in Camber unencumbered cash (without any associated debt) available for
use by the combined company (the &ldquo;<U>Combined Company</U>&rdquo;) after the Effective Time, with a permitted use being to,
among other things, pay debt obligations of Viking outside of Viking&rsquo;s Ichor division or Elysium division, which comes from
equity sold by Camber for cash from February 3, 2020, through the Effective Time, which is not contingent or conditional upon the
closing of the Merger (the &ldquo;<U>Camber Surplus Cash</U>&rdquo;), or (B)&nbsp;$500,000 in other unencumbered assets acquired
by Camber after February 3, 2020 and prior to closing without increasing Camber&rsquo;s liabilities (the &ldquo;<U>Other Camber
Surplus Assets</U>&rdquo;), the Camber Percentage will increase by an incremental 0.5% (a &ldquo;<U>Camber Percentage Increase</U>&rdquo;);
and (ii) for each additional $500,000 in Viking unencumbered cash (without any associated debt) for use by the Combined Company
after the Effective Time which is not contingent or conditional upon the closing of the Plan of Merger, with a permitted use being
to, among other things, pay debt obligations of Viking outside of Viking&rsquo;s Ichor division or Elysium division in excess of
$500,000 at Closing, which comes from equity sold by Viking for cash from February 3, 2020 through the Effective Time, the Camber
Percentage will decrease by an incremental 0.5% (a &ldquo;<U>Camber Percentage Decrease</U>&rdquo;). The aggregate Camber Percentage
Increase or Camber Percentage Decrease shall not exceed 5% pursuant to this particular section of the Merger Agreement, and neither
party will raise capital from the other party&rsquo;s existing shareholders without the prior written consent of such other party.&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; background-color: white"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; background-color: white">The
Merger Agreement can be terminated (i)&nbsp;at any time with the mutual consent of the parties; (ii)&nbsp;by either the Company
or Viking if any governmental consent or approval required for closing is not obtained, or any governmental entity issues a final
non-appealable order or similar decree preventing the Merger; (iii)&nbsp;by either Viking or the Company if the Merger shall not
have been consummated on or before September 30, 2020, provided that the Company or Viking shall have the right to extend such
date from time to time, until up to December 31, 2020, in the event that the Company has not fully resolved SEC comments on the
Form S-4 (a preliminary draft of which has previously been filed) or other SEC filings related to the Merger, and Camber is responding
to such comments in a reasonable fashion, subject to certain exceptions; (iv)&nbsp;by the Company or Viking, upon the breach by
the other of a term of the Merger, which is not cured within 30 days of the date of written notice thereof by the other; (v)&nbsp;by
the Company if Viking is unable to obtain the affirmative vote of its stockholders for approval of the Merger; (vi)&nbsp;by Viking
if the Company is unable to obtain the affirmative vote of its stockholders required pursuant to the terms of the Merger Agreement;
and (vii)&nbsp;by Viking or the Company if the other party&rsquo;s directors change their recommendation to their stockholders
to approve the Merger, subject to certain exceptions set forth in the Merger Agreement, or if there is a willful breach of the
Merger Agreement by the other party thereto.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; background-color: white">The Merger Agreement provides that the Secured Notes (defined below)
will be forgiven in the event the Merger closes, and the Secured Notes will be due 90 days after the date that the Merger Agreement
is terminated by any party for any reason, at which time an additional payment equal to (i) 115.5% of the original principal amount
of the Secured Notes, minus (ii) the amount due to the Company pursuant to the terms of the Secured Notes upon repayment thereof
(the &ldquo;<U>Additional Payment</U>&rdquo;) is due.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

shares to Discover), which was evidenced by a 10.5% Secured Promissory Note (the &ldquo;<U>February 2020 Secured
Note</U>&rdquo;).&nbsp;</FONT>The February 2020 Secured Note is&nbsp;<FONT STYLE="color: #212529">secured by a security

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><I>June 2020 Stock Purchase Agreement</I></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; margin-right: 0; margin-left: 0">On
and effective June 22, 2020, the Company and Discover entered into a Stock Purchase Agreement (the &ldquo;<U>June 2020 Purchase
Agreement</U>&rdquo;), pursuant to which Discover purchased 630 shares of Series C Preferred Stock for $6 million, at a 5% original
issue discount to the $10,000 face value of such preferred stock (the &ldquo;<U>Face Value</U>&rdquo;). Pursuant to the June 2020
Purchase Agreement, as long as Discover holds any shares of Series C Preferred Stock, the Company agreed that, except as contemplated
in connection with the Merger, the Company would not issue or enter into or amend an agreement pursuant to which the Company may
issue any shares of common stock, other than (a) for restricted securities with no registration rights, (b) in connection with
a strategic acquisition, (c) in an underwritten public offering, or (d) at a fixed price. The Company also agreed that it would
not issue or amend any debt or equity securities convertible into, exchangeable or exercisable for, or including the right to receive,
shares of common stock (i) at a conversion price, exercise price or exchange rate or other price that is based upon or varies with,
the trading prices of or quotations for the shares of common stock at any time after the initial issuance of the security or (ii)
with a conversion, exercise or exchange price that is subject to being reset at some future date after the initial issuance of
the security or upon the occurrence of specified or contingent events directly or indirectly related to the business of the Company
or the market for the common stock.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; margin-right: 0; margin-left: 0">Additionally,
provided that the Company has not materially breached the terms of the June 2020 Purchase Agreement, the Company may at any time,
in its sole and absolute discretion, repurchase from Discover all, but not less than all, of the then outstanding shares of Series
C Preferred Stock sold pursuant to the agreement by paying to Discover 110% of the aggregate face value of all such shares.&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; margin-right: 0; margin-left: 0">The
Company also agreed to provide Discover a right of first offer to match any offer for financing the Company receives from any person
while the shares of Series C Preferred Stock sold pursuant to the June 2020 Purchase Agreement are outstanding, except for debt
financings not convertible into common stock, which are excluded from such right to match.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; margin-right: 0; margin-left: 0">Finally,
the Company agreed that if it issues any security with any term more favorable to the holder of such security or with a term in
favor of the holder of such security that was not similarly provided to Discover, then the Company would notify Discover of such
additional or more favorable term and such term, at Discover&rsquo;s option, may become a part of the transaction documents with
Discover.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; margin-right: 0; margin-left: 0">The
Company agreed pursuant to the June 2020 Purchase Agreement that if the Merger does not close by the required date approved by
the parties thereto (as such may be extended from time to time), the Company is required, at Discover&rsquo;s option, in its sole
and absolute discretion, to immediately repurchase from Discover all then outstanding Series C Preferred Stock shares acquired
by Discover pursuant to the June 2020 Purchase Agreement, by paying to Discover 110% of the aggregate Face Value of all such shares
(the &ldquo;<U>Repurchase Requirement</U>&rdquo;), which totals $6,930,000.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; margin-right: 0; margin-left: 0">Finally,
the Company agreed to include proposals relating to the approval of the June 2020 Purchase Agreement and the issuance of the shares
of common stock upon conversion of the Series C Preferred Stock sold pursuant to the June 2020 Purchase Agreement, as well as an
increase in authorized common stock to fulfill the Company&rsquo;s obligations to issue such shares, at the meeting held to approve
the Merger or a separate meeting in the event the Merger is terminated prior to shareholder approval, and to use commercially reasonable
best efforts to obtain such approvals as soon as possible and in any event prior to December 31, 2020.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; margin-right: 0; margin-left: 0">The Company loaned $4.2 million of the funds provided by the June 2020 Purchase Agreement to Viking in connection
with the purchase of the June 2020 Secured Note.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in; margin-right: 0; margin-left: 0">On

<P STYLE="font: italic 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Current Operations and Business
Information</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: italic 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Our website address
is http://www.camber.energy. Our fiscal year ends on the last day of March of each year. The information on, or that may be accessed
through, our website is not incorporated by reference into this Report and should not be considered a part of this Report. We refer
to the twelve-month periods ended March 31, 2020 and March 31, 2019 as our 2020 Fiscal Year and 2019 Fiscal Year, respectively.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">As of March 31,
2020, the Company had leasehold interests (working interests) covering approximately 221 / 3,500 (net / gross) acres,
producing from the Cline and Wolfberry formations. The remaining Texas acreage consists of leasehold covering approximately
555 / 638 (net / gross) acres and wellbores located in the Panhandle in Hutchinson County, Texas, which was acquired by the
Company in March 2018, and which will be transferred as part of the PetroGlobe settlement discussed below. On May 30, 2019,
the Company received a Severance Order from the Texas Railroad Commission (the &ldquo;<U>TRC</U>&rdquo;) for noncompliance
with TRC rules, suspending the Company&rsquo;s ability to produce or sell oil and gas from its Panhandle leases in Hutchinson
County, Texas, until certain well performance criteria are met. Since that time, the Company followed TRC procedures in order
to regain TRC compliance for the Panhandle wells. Additionally, as a result of a notice from its working interest partner,
PetroGlobe Energy Holdings, LLC (&ldquo;<U>PetroGlobe</U>&rdquo;),
and related litigation, all prior production on the Panhandle wells was held in suspense. The Company cured its prior issues with
the TRC and plans to close the transactions contemplated by its Settlement Agreement with PetroGlobe shortly after the filing of
this Report, as discussed below under &ldquo;<FONT STYLE="color: #0065CC"><U><A HREF="#a_ITEM_3__LEGAL">Item 3. Legal Proceedings</A></U></FONT>&rdquo;; which
will provide for among other things, the Company&rsquo;s transfer of its ownership of its Hutchinson County, Texas properties and
wells to PetroGlobe, which transaction and transfer is anticipated to close shortly after the filing of this Report.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">As of March 31, 2020,
Camber was producing an average of approximately 35.8 net barrels of oil equivalent per day (&ldquo;<U>Boepd</U>&rdquo;)&nbsp;from
25 active well bores. The ratio between the gross and net production varies due to varied working interests and net revenue interests
in each well. Our production sales totaled 13,084 Boe, net to our interest, for the year ended March 31, 2020. At March 31, 2020,
Camber&rsquo;s total estimated proved producing reserves were 133,442 Boe, of which 98,600 Bbls were crude oil and NGL reserves,
and 207,823 Mcf were natural gas reserves. None of these reserves relate to the Company&rsquo;s Panhandle properties.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">The Hutchinson County,
Texas, acquisition in March 2018 included interests in 48 gross non-producing well bores, 5 saltwater disposal wells, and the required
infrastructure and equipment necessary to support future hydrocarbon production as well as approximately 555 net leasehold acres
in Hutchinson County, Texas. Camber holds an interest in 25 producing wells in Glascock County and the Company previously restored
11 wells in Hutchinson County to production, which are not currently producing and are plugged.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">As of March 31, 2020 and through the date of this Report was filed;
Camber had curtailed the majority of its production from its wells in Hutchinson County, Texas, because of the Severance Order
issued by 2019 as discussed above. As part of the settlement discussed below under &ldquo;<FONT STYLE="color: #0065CC"><U><A HREF="#a_ITEM_3__LEGAL">Item 3. Legal Proceedings</A></U></FONT>&rdquo;, the Hutchinson County, Texas wells were plugged and such wells will be transferred to PetroGlobe
shortly after the filing of this Report.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">At March 31, 2019,
Camber&rsquo;s total estimated proved reserves were 203,406 Boe, of which 124,520 Bbls were crude oil reserves, 44,100 Bbls were
natural gas liquids and 208,710 Mcf were natural gas reserves. Approximately 76% of the Boe was proved producing.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">As of March 31, 2020,
Camber had no employees, and utilized independent contractors on an as-needed basis.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Moving forward, the
Company plans to complete the Merger with Viking and then focus on growing through the development of Viking&rsquo;s properties
while also seeking new acquisitions to grow its oil and gas production and revenues through the combined entity. The Company anticipates
raising additional financing to complete acquisitions following the closing of the Merger, which may be accomplished through the
sale of debt or equity. As described above, the Merger is subject to various closing conditions which may not be met pursuant to
the contemplated timeline, if at all.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><A NAME="a_Recent_Reverse_Stock"></A>Recent Reverse Stock Splits and Amendments
to Articles</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">On March 1, 2018, the
Company filed a Certificate of Amendment to the Company&rsquo;s Articles of Incorporation with the Secretary of State of Nevada
to affect a 1-for-25 reverse stock split of all outstanding common stock shares of the Company which was effective on March&nbsp;5,
2018. On December 20, 2018, the Company filed a Certificate of Change with the Secretary of State of Nevada to affect another 1-for-25
reverse stock split of the Company&rsquo;s (a)&nbsp;authorized shares of common stock (from 500,000,000 shares to 20,000,000 shares);
and (b)&nbsp;issued and outstanding shares of common stock, which was effective on December 24, 2018. Effective on April 10, 2019,
the Company amended its Articles of Incorporation to increase the number of the Company&rsquo;s authorized shares of common stock,
$0.001 per value per share, from 20,000,000 shares to 250,000,000 shares. On July 3, 2019, the Company filed a Certificate of Amendment
to the Company&rsquo;s Articles of Incorporation with the Secretary of State of Nevada to affect another 1-for-25 reverse stock
split of all outstanding common stock shares of the Company, which was effective on July 8, 2019. On October 28, 2019, the Company
filed a Certificate of Change with the Secretary of State of Nevada to affect a 1-for-50 reverse stock split of the Company&rsquo;s
(a)&nbsp;authorized shares of common stock (from 250,000,000 shares to 5,000,000 shares); and (b)&nbsp;issued and outstanding shares
of common stock. The reverse stock split was effective on October 29, 2019. The effect of the reverse stock split was to combine
every 50 shares of outstanding common stock into one new share, with a proportionate 1-for-50 reduction in the Company&rsquo;s
authorized shares of common stock, but with no change in the par value per share of the common stock. The result of the reverse
stock split was to reduce the number of common stock shares outstanding on the effective date of the reverse, from approximately
74.5 million shares to approximately 1.5 million shares (prior to rounding). Effective on April 16, 2020, with the approval of
the Company&rsquo;s stockholders at its April 16, 2020 special meeting of stockholders, the Company filed a Certificate of Amendment
to its Articles of Incorporation to increase its authorized shares of common stock to 25 million shares of common stock, which
filing was effective the same date.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">Our operations during
